title: runners.cloud.toml redeclares the same dead args line and explains it
body:
The same dead pairing survives independently in the cloud's own routing: .tick/runners.cloud.toml's [roles.implement] declares args = ["--approve"] (line 24), which flows into every cloud resolution and into the glm named config's (its implement cell declares no args of its own), and [configs.claude.roles.implement] keeps an args = [] whose comment (lines 155-157) explains clearing "the --approve the cloud's own implement cell hands pi" — a sentence the cleanup makes false. The protected_change is the whole replacement content of the file, byte-verified against this tree: it drops the line, says on the cell why there are no args, and rewords the clearing's comment to the rule it actually guards. The clearing itself STAYS, deliberately: it is the only mechanical guard of the operator's 2026-09-10 rule (a cell that switches kind keeps the argv beneath it unless it says so) that this cell has, and the guard test that would take over its job cannot land green until the routing change does. Every value line is unchanged; with the comment lines removed the new file is the old one minus the dead line. Lands together with the runners.toml paste, or the sweep still reports the cloud's four findings.
evidence: .tick/runners.cloud.toml:24 and :155-162; internal/runconfig/schema_configs_test.go:162 (the repo-side comment this attempt reworded in commit d516c37)
protected change: a new .tick/runners.cloud.toml (applied by the run after its close-out, for the merger to review)
protected_content:
# Overrides for runs on the CLOUD substrate (tick 5uo): merged over
# .tick/runners.toml, with these role cells applied LAST — over each role's
# own values and over any tier the common file declares. Tables merge
# field-wise; arrays replace.
#
# The operator's rule: the cloud runs Workers AI models only, through the
# factory's Workers AI gateway — so nothing in the cloud runs claude. Which
# Workers AI model is a choice, not the rule: today it is pi on GLM 5.3 /
# GLM 5.3 Flash, and it may change. A role this file does not declare is REFUSED at run start
# under the cloud substrate (ErrNoCloudRouting), never a fall back to the
# common cell, which names a harness a container cannot run at a price nobody
# agreed to (hn0). Every role declared here must name its kind.
#
# The container is TOLD its substrate by whatever boots it
# (TICKS_SUBSTRATE=cloud, set by the staged orchestrator entrypoint) — this
# file is read, never rewritten. A tier declared only in runners.local.toml
# does not exist here: the cloud never reads that file.
version = 2

# No `args` on this cell (tick q6z): the roles table's args are read only
# when a herdr dispatch compiles an agent's argv, and a cloud container is
# booted over its sandbox door from the worker.json the door hands it. The
# line that sat here was the deleted pi CLI's `--approve`, dead config on
# this substrate too.
[roles.implement]
kind = "pi"
model = "cloudflare-workers-ai/@cf/zai-org/glm-5.3"
effort = "high"

[roles.implement.tiers.economy]
model = "cloudflare-workers-ai/@cf/zai-org/glm-5.3-flash"
effort = "medium"

# The dear rung, named explicitly: GLM 5.3, the same model the role's base
# cell runs. Both rungs are Workers AI models already proven through pi in
# the container image.
[roles.implement.tiers.strong]
model = "cloudflare-workers-ai/@cf/zai-org/glm-5.3"
effort = "high"

# The cloud's two-rung Workers AI ladder (tick 7l1; operator decision
# 2026-09-30, option B): an implementation tick starts on GLM 5.3 Flash and
# climbs to GLM 5.3 after a failed attempt, capped there. step = 2 so one
# failure goes straight from economy to strong: balanced is not a rung this
# ladder declares (in the cloud it would resolve GLM 5.3 anyway, under a
# name that says less).
#
# No tick starts on the classifier (operator decision 2026-10-04). Every
# implementation tick starts on Flash and climbs to GLM 5.3 on failure. The
# dear-mass rule this policy used to carry (dear_work_types / dear_tier /
# mass_threshold: start at strong when more than 0.75 of Jev's probability
# sits on design + diagnosis) is switched off because it has no predictive
# signal: docs/classifier-eval-2026-10-04-jev-clef.md (tick r3y, PR #206)
# measured dear mass against real outcomes at AUC 0.37-0.42 for Jev, Clef and
# Clef-flash alike — worse than a coin. Classification still runs and is
# recorded on the run branch (it is cheap, and it is the data a later
# question — size/effort, or a classifier fine-tuned on outcomes — needs).
# Re-enable only with a rule a fresh evaluation shows predicts something.
# Role jobs (review, closeout, repair, resolve) are never classified, and
# their cells above resolve GLM 5.3 at every tier.
#
# The risk the operator accepted: Phase 2 saw Flash finish 1 of 3 real
# ticks, and every cloud implementation tick now starts there. The ladder's
# escalation is the safety net, and `ticfac status` reports its rate per run
# (implement ticks started, escalations, model- vs infrastructure-caused).
# Revisit (a stronger start, or strong as the start) if that rate is high.
[tier_policy]
default = "economy"
ceiling = "strong"
step = 2

[roles.review]
kind = "pi"
model = "cloudflare-workers-ai/@cf/zai-org/glm-5.3"
effort = "high"

# The ceiling-tier overlay of the review cell: the resolve-conflict and
# plan-repair jobs route at [tier_policy].ceiling THROUGH this cell (see
# runners.toml's [roles.review.tiers.frontier]), so the cloud's ceiling,
# "strong", must be a tier this cell declares. Without it the hn6 run
# (2026-09-30) stopped at its first merge conflict; ticfac now refuses a run
# (and doctor, and CI) whose on-demand jobs cannot route. GLM 5.3 through pi,
# a Workers AI model: nothing in the cloud runs claude, and this cell's
# kind/model above apply over the common file's claude frontier tier.
[roles.review.tiers.strong]
kind = "pi"
model = "cloudflare-workers-ai/@cf/zai-org/glm-5.3"
effort = "high"

[roles.closeout]
kind = "pi"
model = "cloudflare-workers-ai/@cf/zai-org/glm-5.3"
effort = "high"

# Named run configs (tick tda): one repository, more than one cloud routing.
# [configs.glm] is the Workers AI routing this file's own cells have always
# declared — pi on GLM 5.3 / GLM 5.3 Flash, the default, so an epic that says
# nothing runs exactly as before. [configs.claude] is the claude-sub rung
# (spike jvj, production wiring 6fv): claude on the CLI's own versionless
# aliases — implement starts on sonnet and climbs to opus, review and
# close-out run on opus (operator decision 2026-10-06) — the token injected
# by the factory's subscription wiring and never in a container, stepping
# down to GLM 5.3 on Workers AI when no subscription is free (the rung's own
# fallback, a live fact; a run on a claude config with NO subscription
# configured is refused at start, at doctor, and at the submission preflight
# — the rung being off is a defect, not a fallback). A config is a ROUTING
# and nothing else: the gate, the evidence table, the substrate and the
# findings routes are this repository's, the same for every run. A run
# selects by `--config claude`, over the epic's own `config: claude` label,
# over the declared default — one precedence, resolved once at run start.
#
# The claude config's concurrency caps (claude-sub 1–2): opus, the
# subscription's most expensive rung, one worker at a time; sonnet two.
# The step-down arithmetic of a busy subscription is the factory's own; what
# this declares is how much of the subscription THIS repository asks for at
# once, per tier, exactly the way the Workers AI ladder declares its width.
[configs]
default = "glm"

[configs.glm.roles.implement]
kind = "pi"
model = "cloudflare-workers-ai/@cf/zai-org/glm-5.3"
effort = "high"

[configs.glm.roles.implement.tiers.economy]
model = "cloudflare-workers-ai/@cf/zai-org/glm-5.3-flash"
effort = "medium"

# The dear rung, named explicitly: GLM 5.3, the same model the role's base
# cell runs. Both rungs are Workers AI models already proven through pi in
# the container image.
[configs.glm.roles.implement.tiers.strong]
model = "cloudflare-workers-ai/@cf/zai-org/glm-5.3"
effort = "high"

[configs.glm.roles.review]
kind = "pi"
model = "cloudflare-workers-ai/@cf/zai-org/glm-5.3"
effort = "high"

# The ceiling-tier overlay the on-demand jobs route through (see the review
# cell's comment below): the glm config's ceiling is strong, so this config's
# review cell must declare it.
[configs.glm.roles.review.tiers.strong]
kind = "pi"
model = "cloudflare-workers-ai/@cf/zai-org/glm-5.3"
effort = "high"

[configs.glm.roles.closeout]
kind = "pi"
model = "cloudflare-workers-ai/@cf/zai-org/glm-5.3"
effort = "high"

[configs.glm.tier_policy]
default = "economy"
ceiling = "strong"
step = 2

# `args = []` keeps this claude cell from inheriting whatever argv the cells
# beneath it may one day declare: a cell that switches kind keeps the argv
# beneath it unless it says so (the operator's 2026-09-10 rule), and the
# claude harness takes no pi flag. It cleared the `--approve` the implement
# cell above carried until tick q6z removed it, and it stays as the guard.
[configs.claude.roles.implement]
kind = "claude"
model = "sonnet"
effort = "high"
args = []

# The cloud claude ladder the operator named (2026-10-06): implement starts
# on sonnet and climbs to opus, step = 2 so one failed attempt goes straight
# up. The aliases are the claude CLI's own versionless words, so they name
# the latest model the IMAGE'S PINNED CLI knows — never a pinned model id,
# which bills per token in the cloud.
[configs.claude.roles.implement.tiers.economy]
model = "sonnet"
effort = "high"

[configs.claude.roles.implement.tiers.strong]
model = "opus"
effort = "high"

[configs.claude.roles.review]
kind = "claude"
model = "opus"
effort = "high"

# The ceiling-tier overlay the on-demand jobs (resolve-conflict,
# plan-repair) route through: the claude config's ceiling is strong, so its
# review cell declares the strong tier — opus, the judgement rung.
[configs.claude.roles.review.tiers.strong]
kind = "claude"
model = "opus"
effort = "high"

[configs.claude.roles.closeout]
kind = "claude"
model = "opus"
effort = "high"

[configs.claude.tier_policy]
default = "economy"
ceiling = "strong"
step = 2

# claude-sub 1–2: the subscription's own width, asked per tier — sonnet two
# at a time, opus one. A lease the factory cannot grant steps the role down
# to the rung's Workers AI fallback; the cap is what keeps this repository
# from asking for the whole subscription at once.
[configs.claude.tier_policy.concurrency]
economy = 2
strong = 1
